subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.
reasoning:
I'm sketching a compact but detailed design: a six-wheeled, three-axle heavy carrier about 9 meters long and 3 meters wide, with deployed outrigger stabilizer legs bracing against the ground while a long forward-pointing railgun sits elevated on a turret mount.

Now I'm working out the skeleton and joint structure—chassis root, turret yaw, gun pitch, outrigger legs, wheel spin joints, and front steering—keeping it minimal using only three.js and a small glow kit import. I'm placing the wheel axles along the length of the hull, laying out the lower chassis box, wheel arches, main deck, and a raked front cab, then shaping the rear armored deck and turret ring where the railgun cradle mounts at a slight upward pitch.

Now I'm designing the four outrigger legs at the chassis corners, each with a hinge joint, an arm extending sideways, and a vertical leg down to a ground pad with a cylindrical foot.

Then I'm deciding to raise the wheel centers slightly off the ground so the outrigger pads become the lowest touching points, and planning the wheel details with tire, rim, hub, lug bolts, and a spin joint along the y-axis.

Building the tread blocks per wheel and setting up a camo-style paint mottled between olive drab and tan with hazard yellow stripes and cyan glow accents for the railguns.

I'm planning the texture decals (unit numbers, hazard stripes, HUD screens, warning labels) and all the physical details—cab windows, sensor dome, stowage boxes, turret with gun capacitor drums and glowing rail gaps, plus rear ammo tray and tow hook.

Writing builder joints and hull geometry...

I'm sizing the hull at roughly 2.4 wide centered between the wheels, spanning about 6.6 in length, then placing the cab box forward of center with its own width matching the hull so it clears the front wheels, topped with a roof and an angled windscreen panel.

Now I'm working out the hood and bumper geometry leading to the front, then shifting to the gun assembly: positioning the pitch mount above the deck, a turret ring and yaw drum stacked on top, cheek plates flanking the gun, and twin rails running nearly the full length of the hull to support it.

Adding the glow strip between the rails, capacitor drums with glow rings along the sides, the breech block at the rear of the gun, and a muzzle bracket with glow discs at the front end.

I'm placing coil rings as cyan-glowing toruses spaced along the barrel, confirming the pitch bone hierarchy so the gun parts build level then pose correctly, with yaw controlling the turret top and pitch controlling the gun itself. Now I'm setting up the texture for the unit number plate.

Working out plane orientation and readability for the "R-6" hull plate text, I'm reasoning through which axis maps to the viewer's right when looking at the +x face, accepting some uncertainty about mirroring. Now I'm moving on to designing hazard stripe textures for the legs and bumper.

Beyond that, I'm planning additional details: a glowing HUD screen on the rear hull panel, an emblem decal for the turret sides, warning triangle markings on the legs, and headlight glow boxes near the front, while working out exact box coordinates for the cab and bumper to position everything correctly.

Now I'm adding greebles -- a roof light bar, two antenna whips, a sensor dome, exhaust stacks with capped pipes behind the cab, and side stowage boxes positioned between the wheels along the hull.

I'm trying to work out leg placement so the outriggers and stowage boxes don't collide with the wheel positions, testing rear legs around z=-3.9 and front legs offset enough to clear the front wheel's radius.

Resolving the overlap by raising the stowage box above the arm height so they clear each other, then working out the leg joint geometry: piston cylinders, pad, and ball joint dimensions, plus naming conventions for the outrigger and leg joints.

Now I'm adding deck surface details—panel lines, hatches, vents, ammo containers, handrails, and a tow hook—then setting up paint helpers for mottled body color and solid dark accents before writing the geometry helper functions.

Writing part/box helpers...

Still writing wheel assembly...

Positioning fenders over the wheels so they overlap the hull slightly while staying clear of it, deciding against a full side skirt and opting for a short front/back lip instead. Now I'm turning to cab details—windshield glass, side windows, door lines, mirror arms, wipers, a roof light bar, and headlight glow at the front.

Working out the nose geometry: a sloped frustum between the cab front and the lower nose, headlights and a dark grille box on the nose face, and a hazard-striped bumper with proper ground clearance, plus tow hooks. Now I'm positioning the windscreen as a tilted box in front of the cab, working out the correct rotation angle so the top edge leans back realistically.

I'm placing the side window boxes, roof slab, and roof sensor, and settling the API for spikes and rods (base point, direction/tip, length, radius, color, bone options) to use for the antenna and handrail along the deck. I'm also noting the dome uses a partial sphere geometry for a flat-bottomed look, and that textures from SVG can be passed into parts via a texture property.

I'm deciding to skip the lathe geometry for the muzzle brake and sensor dome to keep things simple, and planning the final code structure: imports from the builder library and glow kit, the chassis root joint position, and hydraulic ram rods connecting the hull to the gun cradle across the yaw and pitch bones.
